 Education ministers announce suite of curriculum reforms, new commission
 by 
 Meg Kennedy 
 November 5, 2026 
 in 
 Curriculum , Latest News , Policy and Reform 
 Reading Time: 3 mins read
 A 
 A 
 A 
 A 
 Reset 
 Image: Phillip Minnis/Adobe Stock
 Education ministers have agreed to a “digital detox” in Australian schools and a package of reforms, aimed to strengthen children’s learning and support teachers. 
 Following the Education Ministers Meeting on Monday 2 November, ministers agreed to: a digital detox in Australian schools; curriculum reform to strengthen the teaching of Australian mathematics and financial literacy and antisemitism; looking to make civics compulsory in Years 9 and 10; and the establishment of the Australian Teaching and Learning Commission.
 Digital detox
 According to statement from Education Minister Mr Jason Clare, education ministers have agreed to set or consider screen-time limits in schools, alongside restricting the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in primary schools and secondary school assessments.
 A new Australian Schools Digital Detox Taskforce will provide advice on further steps to address excessive screen time and digital device use. According to Mr Clare, the taskforce will collect evidence, survey students, teachers and parents, and provide ministers with advice on what further action to take into 2027.
 Ministers also decided to return NAPLAN writing tests in Year 5 to pen-and-paper , from 2028.
 Curriculum changes
 Next year will see changes to the curriculum for the first three years of mathematics. Ministers have tasked ACARA with the next targeted curriculum review, looking at the mathematics curriculum for Years 3 to 6, including a bigger focus on financial literacy.
 “We have signed long-term agreements with every state and territory to fix the funding of our public schools. That funding is tied to reforms that we know work: things like phonics and phonics checks, numeracy checks and small group tutoring,” said Mr Clare.
 Democracy will also be in the spotlight, with ministers asking ACARA to provide advice of making Civics and Citizenship content compulsory across the country in Years 9 and 10.
 Tackling antisemitism
 The Antisemitism Education Taskforce has endorsed recommendations by ACARA and education ministers, which will start from 2027, including an understanding of Jewish history and culture.
 The Social Cohesion Education Advisory Council, to be chaired by Mr David Gonski, will progress further work to strengthen social cohesion through education. It will also provide advice on how to better embed the teaching of Australian values into the curriculum.
 The Australian Teaching and Learning Commission
 A new single body responsible for the national curriculum, national testing, national teacher standards, teacher training and research will be established.
 Aimed to make it easier and simpler for teachers and schools to get information, resources and support, the Commission will bring under one roof: the Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority (ACARA); the Australian Institute for Teaching and School Leadership (AITSL); the Australian Education Research Organisation (AERO) and Education Services Australia (ESA).
 According to Mr Clare, the Commission would allow for greater coordination between different areas of the school education system, and help support key reforms as part of the Better and Fairer Schools Agreement.
